Today’s release of macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 adds a new dynamic wallpaper of the Golden Gate Bridge, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. All of them are available for download below.

macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpaper gallery continues to expand

When Apple unveiled macOS 27 Golden Gate at WWDC26, the company showed the same system wallpaper across all of its operating systems, featuring a stylised 27.

However, after several developer beta versions, Apple began adding dynamic screensavers that double as wallpapers, featuring serene slow-motion video footage looking toward the iconic Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.

When the Mac is unlocked, the screensaver slowly comes to a halt, and each still wallpaper you pause on will look slightly different.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, below you’ll find static screenshots of the four videos, plus light and dark versions of the stylised 27 wallpaper.

Remember to click on the images to save the full-resolution versions. To set as a background image, go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to Your Photos, click the Add Photo button, then choose any of the following methods:

Add photos from your Photos library: Click Choose from Photos, then pick a photo. Add image files: Click Choose Files, select a file, then click Open. You can also drag images from the desktop or a folder onto the thumbnail at the top of the Wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: Click Choose Folder, pick a folder, then click Open. Add an album or folder from the Photos app: Under Photo Collections, pick an album or folder.

According to Apple, "you can also choose a custom wallpaper without opening Wallpaper settings":

Use a photo from your Photos library: Go to the Photos app, pick a photo, click the Share button in the Photos toolbar, then click Set as Wallpaper. Use an image found online: Control-click an image in a Safari window, then choose Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper. Use an image saved on your Mac: Click Finder in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click Set as Desktop Picture.

To learn more about how to set a custom wallpaper in macOS, follow this link.

Got a favourite? Let us know in the comments.
